conclusion: A bare balanced CMOS push-pull stage is not a complete IF driver and does not meet the 0.378649-ohm 100-MHz output-impedance target within the screened 20-mm effective NMOS width. Its 20-mm bank also presents 78.009 pF at the SS/hot DC trip point; the same linear width extrapolation reaches 903.394 pF. A later multistage feedback driver must therefore model its output-stage gate drive and distribution, power, linearity, common-mode control, and stability before sampler layout.

evidence.actual_screen: 45 complete small-signal AC simulations at the individual DC trip point; widths use 4-um NMOS / 8-um PMOS fingers with multiplicity

gate_drive_load_at_100mhz_with_output_ac.scope: small-signal total common gate capacitance of the balanced PMOS/NMOS output bank; it is an output-stage gate-drive load, not a required gate-swing or gate-drive-current claim

next_required_topology: closed-loop, multistage differential IF power buffer with a separately characterized large output bank and explicit common-mode feedback, gate-drive power, linearity, stability, and 425-pF-or-larger sampled-load PEX
